summary: A July 1933 Florida Times-Union item, quoted on a Forest Lookouts page, reports an 80-foot wooden lookout tower under construction near Dinsmore in Duval County.

facts.design: Wooden fire lookout tower erected with a German-patented wooden joint coupler
facts.status_note: No source found says whether the Dinsmore tower stands today, or whether the site is open to visitors.

events.note: Reported as under construction in July 1933. The item gives no completion date. Height is the 80-foot figure converted to metres.

evidence.supports: 80-foot wooden fire lookout tower under construction near Dinsmore, July 1933
evidence.quote: The 80-foot wooden fire lookout tower under construction near Dinsmore is being built by a method new and unique in the United States

evidence.supports: Statement from the Tallahassee office of State Forester Harry Lee Baker
evidence.quote: statement from the Tallahassee office of Harry Lee Baker, State Forester

evidence.supports: Tower erected with a new wooden joint coupler, a German-patented device; first structure in this country to use it
evidence.quote: A new kind of wooden joint coupler is being used in erecting the tower which will be the first structure to be built in this country using the German-patented device.

evidence.supports: Such couplers had been in use in Europe since the World War
evidence.quote: These couplers, according to the State forester, have been in use in Europe since the World War

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts page files the item under Duval County

sources.title: DINSMORE - FOREST LOOKOUTS (quoting The Florida Times-Union, July 10, 1933)

notes_for_editor: One source: a catalogue page quoting a July 1933 Times-Union item. The item describes a tower under construction, so no completion date or later history is recorded. The story is about 120 words after the fact-check edits, at the floor, with no further evidence found. The brief height of 24.4 m matches the item's 80 feet. Searches found nothing else on a Dinsmore tower. A Jacksonville parks page describes a different 100-foot tower, the Flagler or Southside tower moved by the CCC in 1938, and the FFLA 2015 report says a Jacksonville Heights tower was removed; neither is linked to Dinsmore, so they are not used. The CCC and 200-tower claims from search snippets were not verified and are not used. Access is unknown and no access level is asserted.
